pairs.subject: review-iteration-loops
pairs.evidence: app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:160-171 — the loop is otherwise exemplary (typed notes, shared refusal guards, share-split ledger, re-gate over the chain on screen), but the post-apply gate is lexical only, so no causal connector is re-checked at the seams a cut or insert creates, and the plan's `unchanged` list is parsed and discarded.

techniques.evidence: app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:263-277 shows three candidates side by side, each anchored to a named craft template carrying its own declared direction and weakness (app/_phases/script/renders.ts:9-27), and the pick terminates the phase (_parts/HypothesisColumn.tsx:173); notes then route to a recalibration that emits edits, never a re-run of the slate.

app/_phases/script/ScriptStep.tsx:160-171 re-gates after apply with `gateChains`, a lexical evidence/hedge gate, so no structural invariant is re-checked at a seam: editPlan.ts:146-148 splices a cut beat out and leaves its successor's BUT/THEREFORE connector written for a predecessor that no longer exists, and nothing reports the broken chain.

app/_phases/script/_matrix/MatrixTracks.tsx:97-138 — the artifact is a chain of discrete text beats; the technique's own boundary excludes discrete media, which have no acoustic or visual joint for a seam to fail at.

app/_phases/script/_notes/PresetSelect.tsx:16-18 offers exactly the closed vocabulary defined at versions.ts:40-47 (more-focus / less-focus / descope / move-earlier / move-later plus a custom hatch), each hint naming its minimal operation; _notes/NoteComposer.tsx:80-81 and _notes/RecalibrateControl.tsx:196-198 say per note which ones move nothing rather than implying they moved a bar.

app/_phases/script/_notes/DeclinedList.tsx:24 records four declined kinds and no `considered and unchanged` list, while editPlan.ts:283 parses the plan's `unchanged` array and drops it — so a render the engine deliberately left alone is indistinguishable from one it forgot.

app/_phases/script/_matrix/shared.tsx:44-73 writes the same scope record the triage board reads (no second door), and recalibrate.ts:80-108 refuses a note that would descope required material or re-weight a descoped card — routing it back in the triage board's own wording — with the refusals rendered at _notes/DeclinedList.tsx:42-50 and the conflict's winner named at recalibrate.ts:126-133.

app/_phases/script/_matrix/shared.tsx:101-105 states the sum-to-runtime invariant that impact.ts::splitAcross enforces; _matrix/MatrixSpend.tsx:81-84 shows attributed seconds against the runtime with any overrun named, and shared.tsx:38-42 / 94-99 keeps spoken / cut / unused distinct and reports cut records naming a fact the notebook no longer has.

app/_phases/script/_matrix/shared.tsx:94-99 is the receiving end of a kill, not an interrogation channel; this context has no follow-up queue — evidence doubts route back to the Research step, and the technique forbids routing rendering complaints through it.

pairs.registryProposal: Upward lesson rather than a defect: refusal-as-valid-outcome's refuse-before-apply ordering has no account of a guard that knows its own band is narrower than the rule it enforces. This repo's answer (app/_phases/script/_notes/RecalibrateControl.tsx:13-17,126-136) is that a blocking verdict does not disable the accept button — it makes the click a two-step deliberate act and stamps a permanent override receipt on the version, visible wherever that version is named (_matrix/VersionBar.tsx:33-44). That keeps the guard from becoming the expensive choice without letting the violation go unrecorded, and is worth a technique paragraph or an application with this file:line.

pairs.subject: image-prompt-composition
pairs.evidence: lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:188-192 — the edit path attaches the subject image and up to 13 style references with no role declaration at all, and lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts:141 ships one dialect's prompt verbatim to a different model class on re-route; 8 of 11 techniques have no subject in this layer because the compiler is lib/stylePrompt.ts.

techniques.evidence: lib/imaging/types.ts:76-85 — GenerateRequest carries one opaque prompt string; this context is the vendor transport layer and composes no prompt, so the style/action split has no subject here (it is compiled at lib/stylePrompt.ts:30-65).

lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:342-351 — buildPrompt appends the reference-labelling and exclusion clauses after the caller's prompt rather than prepending them, so the style block the compiler put first stays first and the constraint clause stays last.

lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:342-351 passes the palette through untouched; role assignment is a property of the style block compiled at lib/stylePrompt.ts:23-38, and nothing in this layer reads, rewrites or grades colour.
lib/imaging/types.ts:77 — the subject description arrives already written; this layer never authors or translates a noun, so there is nothing here that could invite or avoid a text magnet.

lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts:142 sends the exclusions as `negative_prompt`, while lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:350 folds the same string into a positive exclusion clause because Google exposes no negative channel — one vendor-neutral contract, two deliveries, exactly the per-vendor adapter the technique asks for.

lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts:45-49,131-135 records the vendor's hard ceiling and enforces it before dispatch as `invalid-request` with a message naming what to shorten, and the fleet minimum is the same 1500 in the compiler (lib/stylePrompt.ts:67) — two copies of one constant is a drift risk, not a missing budget.

lib/imaging/providers/leonardo.ts:141 ships `req.prompt` verbatim to a caption-class diffusion model while providers/google.ts:158 ships the same string to an instruction-following multimodal model; the adapters differ only in negative delivery, so the re-route at router.ts:73 crosses a dialect boundary unrendered — and the 60-cell trial that demoted Leonardo (router.ts:60-72) compared one dialect's prompt across both classes.
lib/imaging/types.ts:77 — the medium vocabulary is authored in the style block (lib/themes.ts, lib/stylePrompt.ts:30-38); this layer neither writes nor audits medium terms.

lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:342-351 — this pipeline is the composited-plate architecture: the no-text clause is welded into the compiler (lib/stylePrompt.ts:43) and every checkable glyph is drawn by the vector layer, so the technique's precondition (the model, not a compositor, sets the text) does not hold.
lib/imaging/types.ts:82-84 — `references` carries approved style plates only; there is no recurring-subject identity block in this layer and no subject conditioning for the split to sit under.

lib/imaging/providers/google.ts:188-192 — the edit path attaches the subject image plus up to 13 style references with no role declaration at all (the generate path's labelling clause at google.ts:344-349 is never applied there, and even on generate the label trails the prompt instead of leading it), so heterogeneous attachments arrive ambiguous about each other.

pairs.registryProposal: Not a defect in the standard — a mapping question. image-prompt-composition governs the prompt COMPILER, and in this repo that is lib/stylePrompt.ts (self-described as 'the one compiler', with restatement, assigned colour roles and the welded no-text clause), lib/themes.ts and app/_phases/frames/shotPrompt.ts — not lib/imaging/*. Eight of eleven techniques have no subject in the mapped paths, and the match looks like vocabulary overlap (prompt / negativePrompt / imaging) rather than the subject's precondition. Suggest re-pointing this subject at the compiler context and keeping only negative-prompting, prompt-budget-limits, prompt-dialect-matching and reference-role-map against the provider layer, since those four are genuinely per-vendor adapter concerns.
